name: Linen grey
lede: Linen grey is a warm, dusty neutral from the Ridgway and ISCC-NBS naming lineage, so close to pink in the 1955 dictionary's own categories that it was filed as a shade of brownish pink, not grey.

sections.title: A grey filed as a pink
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* and the 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary both carry this tone, though neither locator, the exact plate or block, is recorded in our source [1]. What is recorded is a mismatch: the ISCC-NBS category nearest this swatch is brownish pink, about 3.7 units away, not any of the dictionary's grey blocks [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[mauve-blush]] and [[khaki-web]], at [[khaki-web]] sits a little further off, about 4.3 units away and more vivid [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive matches this tone in 2,538 of 23,781 paintings, about 10.67 percent, as photographed, more common than 95 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks early, in the 1100s, present in 16.0 percent of the 50 paintings we have from that century, though that century's sample is thin [3].

Inside a painting it most often plays a light tone, in 42 percent of its 1,800 clearly-ranked appearances, a rank computed within each canvas so varnish cannot fake it [3]. Dutch marine painter Willem van de Velde (I) favors it most, in 5 of his 14 works here, 4.5 times his museums' baseline rate, and it shares canvases with Taupe more than chance alone would predict [3]. In printed English the word "linen grey" peaked in use in the 1870s, though that Ngram count covers every sense of the words, not only the color [3].
